title: Can a Creator Build a House Before Building a Company?
author: RN Collins
principle: Evidence leads; atmosphere never substitutes for provenance.

narrativeSequence.caption: A creator can build institutional capacity before forming a company—method, evidence, relationships, audience routes, promises, and an archive—but should never confuse that capacity with legal personality, liability protection, tax status, or governance.
The house is visible as both maker attribution and an enduring cataloguing unit.

01 · PRACTICE — What already repeats?. Document the offer, client or audience promise, research method, design sequence, collaborator roles, quality threshold, payment path, correction route, and archive habit. Repetition reveals the institution already operating around the person.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 02 · RECORD — Can the practice prove what happened?. Use written scopes, invoices, contributor credits, versioned files, rights and permissions records, contact consent, expense evidence, tax records, and object identifiers appropriate to the actual jurisdiction and activity.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 03 · SEPARATE — Which formal questions cannot be solved by good habits?. Entity formation, liability, tax treatment, employment, insurance, securities, licenses, registrations, beneficial ownership, contracting authority, and cross-border activity require fact-specific professional review. A beautiful archive does not create a liability shield.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 04 · TRANSITION — What should move when structure arrives?. Inventory names, domains, accounts, agreements, equipment, files, marks, designs, licenses, debts, receivables, privacy obligations, and archive custody. Counsel and advisers must determine what can be assigned, licensed, contributed, retained, or newly contracted.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: Universal Electronic Records Management Requirements, Version 3 is retained as evidence, education, reporting or rights context.

frames.caption: Celebrating “institution before company” can romanticize informal work, delay protections, conceal unpaid labor, or expose the creator and collaborators to avoidable risk. The point is not to postpone advice. It is to arrive with a legible practice map—and to formalize when the facts, jurisdiction, liability, tax, labor, funding, and continuity needs require it.

mapping.prompt: Map every recurring promise, role, payment, file, account, right, obligation, and correction route already in use.
Mark the person or entity currently named on each agreement, invoice, domain, account, registration, and insurance record.
List every place where collaborators, customers, money, manufacturing, data, travel, or liability create a professional-review trigger.
Take the transition inventory to qualified legal, tax, insurance, employment, and financial advisers in the relevant jurisdictions.
